Apply for Standalone TPD — discounted as you are happy for TPD to be linked with Life due to premium affordability.
Apply for Income Protection with a shorter benefit period (e.g. 2 or 5 years) — discounted as it does not provide adequate protection.
Apply for Income Protection with a longer waiting period (e.g. 6/12 months) — discounted as you may not have sufficient funds to support you during the waiting period.
Self-insure using your net worth — discounted as your need for insurance exceeds the value of your net worth and you are not comfortable with the inherent level of risk.

modules.trigger: Top-up / increase existing cover

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you top-up your insurance cover through [Insurer] and therefore be insured for the following amounts: [amounts]. We recommend you apply for your top-up insurance cover through [Insurer].
soa.outcomesLine: You will have affordable additional cover that meets your needs, including covering your debts, with appropriate features and benefits to maintain your family and lifestyle.
why: Your full existing personal debt, partial existing/proposed investment debt, and any funeral and final expenses will be covered.
A lump sum has been added to gross up the life cover to allow linking with TPD and Trauma benefits, reducing the overall cost compared with standalone cover.
risks: Your total premiums will increase, however the recommended policies provide for an increase to appropriate sums insured.
Funding insurance premiums from your superannuation will have an impact on your retirement balance estimated at $XXX or XX% over a 5 year period.
alternatives: (uses the standard insurance alternatives above)

modules.trigger: Replace / cancel & take out new cover (with takeover terms)

soa.strategiesLine: [Name], we recommend you cancel your existing insurance and take out new insurance cover and therefore be insured for the following amounts: [amounts]. [Name], we strongly recommend that you apply for the recommended replacement cover and do not cancel your current insurance within [Fund] until the new insurances are in force. This will ensure that if your application is declined for any reason you will still have some insurance in place.
soa.outcomesLine: Once the recommended insurances are in place, cancelling your existing cover consolidates your insurance with one provider, easing administration and avoiding multiple policy fees.
why: The recommended replacement cover provides additional benefits (such as improved definitions and access to trauma insurance) compared to your existing cover.
Your recommended insurance will be underwritten, which means come claim time you know where you stand with a payout; your current cover has never been underwritten, which leaves uncertainty.
Holding consolidated insurance with one provider eases ongoing administration and prevents paying multiple policy fees.
risks: In replacing insurance policies, no two policies are exactly identical — depending on the claim circumstances one policy may provide a better benefit than another. We do not believe there are any significant disadvantages to our recommendation.
There may be restrictions in the new policy or the cover may be accepted on different terms than the existing policy.
You lose any cover you currently hold as soon as it is cancelled — wait to cancel until you receive confirmation from the new insurer.

Suicide (temporary) — as the new policy replaces part of your current cover, you will lose cover in the event of suicide during the first 13 months of the new life cover; this is reinstated once the policy has been in force more than 13 months.
alternatives: Rollover part of your super in order to retain your existing insurance cover within super — discounted as the recommended replacement provides additional benefits, and a partial rollover would leave more than one super account to track.

modules.trigger: Retain existing cover (inside super)

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you retain your existing insurance through [Fund] and remain insured for the following amounts: [amounts]. (Where applicable: [Name], we recommend you retain your existing Life insurance while cancelling your TPD and IP insurances through [Fund].)
soa.outcomesLine: Retaining your existing cover maintains your underwritten terms while keeping premiums funded from super to protect your cashflow.
why: Retains your underwritten Life & TPD insurance.
By holding insurance cover inside superannuation, the cost of the premiums can be met from your superannuation balance, which frees up your cashflow for other purposes.
As much cover as possible is held within the superannuation environment to reduce the effect on your personal cashflow.
risks: If personal insurance cover is held in a superannuation environment, any claim is subject to superannuation release laws (assessment can take time) and proceeds may be subject to tax.
The premium quoted is a guide only; loading can occur following full underwriting.
alternatives: Apply for cover completely outside superannuation — discounted as the premium cost would then need to be met from your everyday income.
Self-insure using your net worth — discounted as your need for insurance exceeds your net worth.

modules.trigger: Income Protection — retain existing

soa.strategiesLine: We have recommended retaining your income protection policy with 75% of your income and super. We have recommended retaining the 13 week wait period as you have available cash and leave to fund 13 weeks of expenses (this reduces the overall cost), and retaining the longest benefit period to ensure maximum coverage across your working life.
soa.outcomesLine: Retaining your income protection maintains your income replacement while keeping the cost efficient.
why: Maintains income replacement to age 65/longest benefit period, ensuring you can afford everyday expenses if unable to work.
risks: Income protection does not fully replace your income (generally not designed to cover 100%), which may create a shortfall in disposable income.
Indemnity cover is subject to assessment of your income prior to claim — if your income has decreased you may receive a lower payout.
alternatives: Apply for IP with a longer waiting period — discounted as you may not have sufficient funds during the waiting period.

modules.trigger: Employer-paid / default cover (retain or note)

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you retain your existing employer-paid (default) insurance cover of [amounts] held within [Fund], in addition to the recommended cover. (Or, where being replaced: we recommend you cancel your default cover within [Fund] once the new underwritten cover is in force.)
soa.outcomesLine: Retaining your employer-paid cover maintains valuable cover at no cost to your cashflow while the recommended underwritten cover provides certainty at claim time.
why: Default cover is provided at no direct cost to you (premiums met by your employer / within the fund) and is generally provided on an automatic-acceptance basis without underwriting.
Retaining it provides an additional layer of cover alongside the recommended underwritten policy.
risks: Default/group cover is not underwritten, so at claim time the insurer may assess pre-existing conditions and exclusions, creating uncertainty. Cover usually ceases if you change employer or your account becomes inactive.
Default cover levels are generic and may not match your actual needs.
alternatives: Cancel the default cover and rely solely on the new underwritten cover — discounted where the default cover provides valuable additional cover at no cashflow cost.

modules.trigger: Apply for child cover

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you take out Child Cover of $XXX for [child/children] under your policy.
soa.outcomesLine: Child Cover provides a lump sum to support your family if a child suffers a defined trauma event, and can later convert to adult cover.
why: Provides a lump sum on a child's defined trauma event to fund medical costs and time away from work.
If the insured child meets the eligibility criteria, they may convert the Child Cover to an equivalent adult Life Insurance Plan without reapplying or providing medical evidence.
risks: Child Cover is limited to defined conditions; some conditions carry a qualifying period.
Premiums add to the overall policy cost.
alternatives: Self-fund a child's medical/recovery costs — discounted where a lump sum provides more certainty.

modules.trigger: Premium structure — stepped vs level / variable age-stepped

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend a Variable Age-Stepped premium structure for all cover. [Couple variant: where a client prefers long-term affordability, recommend a level premium structure for that person, and a variable age-stepped structure for the other.]
soa.outcomesLine: Your premium structure is matched to your affordability preference — variable age-stepped for immediate affordability and flexibility, level for long-term affordability.
why: We have recommended a Variable Age-Stepped premium structure which will give you immediate affordability and ongoing flexibility of your coverage.
[Level variant] We have recommended retaining a level premium structure which will give you long-term affordability.
risks: Premiums increase over time (for stepped / variable age-stepped structures).
Holding cover inside super reduces your retirement balance over time.
Underwriting may apply medical exclusions or loadings (e.g. higher premiums for smoker status); a suicide exclusion typically applies for the first 13 months.
alternatives: Structure all premiums as level. While this would reduce your ongoing premium payable, I have discounted this strategy as premiums would be significantly higher initially making short-term affordability an issue. The recommended insurance structure provides immediate affordability and flexibility in the sum insured.

modules.trigger: Cancel cover no longer required

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you cancel your existing [cover type] of $XXX as it exceeds your current insurance needs.
soa.outcomesLine: Cancelling cover you no longer need removes an unnecessary premium cost, improving your cashflow.
why: Reduces premium outlay where your need for cover has reduced (e.g. debts repaid, assets accumulated, children independent).
risks: Once cancelled you lose the cover immediately; if your circumstances change, new cover would require fresh underwriting and may be more expensive or declined. Do not cancel existing cover until you are certain it is no longer required.
alternatives: Retain the cover — discounted where it clearly exceeds your assessed need and the premium is better directed elsewhere.

modules.trigger: Income Protection — increasing/CPI-indexed claim benefit

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend an increasing-claim option so that, while you are receiving payments, your benefit is indexed at each review date in line with CPI. This increase is capped to 5% if income protection is structured through superannuation.
soa.outcomesLine: Your income protection payments keep pace with inflation during a long claim.
why: The increasing-claim option protects the real value of your benefit payments over a multi-year claim.
risks: The 5% cap (for super-held cover) may not fully match CPI in high-inflation periods; the indexed benefit increases your premium; indexation applies only while you are on claim.
alternatives: Level (non-indexed) benefit — lower ongoing premium but the benefit's real value erodes during a long claim.

modules.trigger: Trauma cover with reinstatement benefit

soa.strategiesLine: We have recommended a trauma reinstatement benefit which allows you to reinstate the trauma benefit after a claim has been paid.
soa.outcomesLine: After a trauma claim is paid, your cover can be reinstated so you remain protected against a later, unrelated trauma event.
why: Recovery from one condition does not remove the risk of a later, unrelated trauma event; reinstatement restores cover for that scenario.
risks: The reinstated benefit may be subject to conditions/waiting periods and adds to the premium; not all insurers offer it.
alternatives: Single-claim trauma cover only — lower cost but no protection against a subsequent event.

modules.trigger: Linked cover with buy-back feature

soa.strategiesLine: As your TPD/Trauma cover is linked to your Life/TPD cover, a claim on one type of cover will reduce the sum insured on the other — we recommend adding the cover buy-back feature so the reduced cover can be reinstated after a claim.
soa.outcomesLine: After a linked claim reduces your other cover, the buy-back feature restores it without re-underwriting.
why: Linked cover is more cost-effective than standalone policies, and the buy-back feature removes the main drawback by restoring the reduced cover after a claim.
risks: The buy-back feature adds to the premium; it applies within defined terms and age limits.
alternatives: Standalone (unlinked) policies — no claim-driven reduction but materially higher premiums; or linked cover without buy-back (cheaper, but cover reduces after a claim).

modules.trigger: Future insurability / guaranteed future increases

soa.strategiesLine: Your recommended policies contain future insurability clauses, meaning that if your circumstances change in future you can increase your cover periodically without further medical underwriting.
soa.outcomesLine: You can raise your cover at set life events or intervals without a new health assessment.
why: This locks in your current health rating, so deterioration in your health does not block reasonable future increases within policy limits.
risks: Increases are limited to set amounts/intervals and have age limits; the increased benefit is still subject to claims assessment.
alternatives: Lock cover at today's level with no increase option — lower flexibility if your needs grow.

modules.trigger: Own-occupation TPD definition
modules.scopeGate: TPD cover recommended for a specialised/high-income occupation

soa.strategiesLine: We have recommended TPD with an 'Own Occupation' definition, which is the highest level of cover.
soa.outcomesLine: A claim can be met if you are unable to work in your own specific occupation, rather than any occupation.
why: Own-occupation cover suits a specialised or high-income role where being unable to perform that specific occupation, even if able to do another, would end your earning capacity.
risks: Own-occupation cover costs more than any-occupation; where linked, a claim reduces the linked cover unless a buy-back feature is added.
alternatives: Any-occupation TPD — cheaper but a narrower claim trigger (must be unable to work in any occupation suited to you).

modules.trigger: Differentiate TPD definition by life stage (own-occ primary earner / any-occ spouse)
modules.scopeGate: Couple with differing work/earning situations (e.g. one on parental leave)

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend own-occupation TPD for the primary earner and retaining any-occupation TPD for the spouse who is currently out of the workforce / on parental leave.
soa.outcomesLine: Cover definition is matched to each person's earning role and stage.
why: The primary earner's income is concentrated in a specific occupation (own-occupation is appropriate); the spouse currently out of the workforce is adequately served by the existing any-occupation cover, which is reviewed on return to work.
risks: Any-occupation has a higher claim hurdle; the spouse's cover should be reviewed and potentially upgraded on return to work.
alternatives: Own-occupation for both — higher cost not warranted while the spouse is out of the workforce.

modules.trigger: Trauma payout deployment (medical recovery + partner salary replacement)
modules.scopeGate: Trauma cover recommended; sum insured sized to a purpose split

soa.strategiesLine: Your trauma cover is sized to cover an estimated amount for medical expenses plus an amount for your partner's salary replacement while you recover (e.g. $125,000 medical + the balance for partner salary replacement).
soa.outcomesLine: The lump sum is explicitly sized to fund both your treatment/recovery costs and your partner's time off work to support you.
why: Segmenting the trauma sum insured into medical-recovery and partner-salary-replacement components ensures the household keeps running while you recover.
risks: The actual split needed may differ from the estimate; 'Plus' features may cap per condition.
alternatives: Standalone trauma plus separate income protection for the partner — duplicates cost.

modules.trigger: Retain cover during workforce absence (maternity / parental leave)
modules.scopeGate: One person temporarily out of the workforce (e.g. parental leave)

soa.strategiesLine: While you are not working, we recommend you retain your existing in-super insurance cover (Life/TPD/IP) at its current levels, with the income protection structured with a shorter waiting period funded by available cash and leave, and we will reassess cover levels once you return to the workforce.
soa.outcomesLine: Cover continuity is preserved through the leave period without re-underwriting, and is reviewed when income normalises.
why: Retaining cover during leave preserves your future insurability and avoids re-underwriting on return to work.
We are not recommending an increase in cover at this time given your cashflow while on leave; we will reassess once you have returned to work.
risks: You may be temporarily under-insured relative to your full needs analysis during the leave period; income protection may be limited while not earning.
alternatives: Cancel cover and re-apply on return — discounted due to re-underwriting cost, delay and the risk of a health change in the interim.

modules.trigger: Retain existing cover and top up with new cover
modules.scopeGate: Transitional period (e.g. workforce re-entry) where flexibility is wanted

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you retain your existing cover and top up with new recommended cover.
soa.outcomesLine: You keep tax-effective in-super cover while adding flexible personal cover that can be adjusted later.
why: A small in-super retention is 'sticky' and tax-effective; the additional personal cover maintains optionality during a transitional period.
risks: Two policies mean more administration; the new cover must remain affordable after your circumstances settle.
alternatives: All new cover inside super — simpler but less flexible and locks in super deductions.

modules.trigger: Cancel cover no longer required (age + debt-free + income-replacement redundant)
modules.scopeGate: Approaching/at retirement, debt cleared, no income to protect

soa.strategiesLine: By completing a full rollover of your existing super fund, your existing Life, TPD & Income Protection insurance will be cancelled. Due to your age and future lack of debt, we believe you do not require this or any other personal insurance going forward, and recommend you cancel your existing cover.
soa.outcomesLine: Premiums no longer erode your balance once cover is no longer needed.
why: With no debt, no dependants relying on your income, and retirement income in place, personal insurance is no longer required, and cancelling it preserves your capital.
risks: If your circumstances change (e.g. new dependants), you may be unable to re-acquire cover at the same rates; ensure cover is genuinely no longer needed before cancelling.
alternatives: Retain partial cover via a partial rollover — discounted as it leaves more than one super account and ongoing premiums for cover you no longer require.

modules.trigger: Dual income protection — retail top-up over employer/industry cover (offset benefit)
modules.scopeGate: Existing employer/industry-fund IP retained, with a retail policy added to top up

soa.strategiesLine: You will have two income protection policies (your existing fund cover plus the recommended retail policy). The retail policy is designed to top up the cover provided by your fund so that you receive up to 70% of your income. In the event of a claim you cannot receive the full benefit from both — the retail payout reduces by the amount paid from your fund cover.
soa.outcomesLine: Your total income protection reaches ~70% of income at the lowest cost, by topping up rather than duplicating existing cover.
why: Retaining the existing fund cover and topping it up is cheaper than replacing it entirely.
Where the existing cover has no pre-existing medical exclusions, keeping it means a condition excluded on the new retail policy may still be claimable under the retained cover.
risks: The two policies overlap and benefits offset — you cannot stack both to exceed the insured percentage; coordination is required at claim time.
alternatives: Single standalone retail policy — simpler but more expensive and forfeits the no-exclusions benefit of the retained cover.

modules.trigger: Occupation pre-assessment / high-risk occupation constraint
modules.scopeGate: Client in a high-risk / manual occupation affecting insurability

soa.strategiesLine: Given your occupation, an occupation pre-assessment was completed for this plan. As your role is considered high risk, the recommended insurer is the only one offering full benefits — other insurers either do not provide TPD/Income Protection or offer Income Protection with a shorter benefit period. Where your occupation caps cover (e.g. income protection limited to a set monthly amount, a shorter benefit period and no super contribution option), we have recommended cover within those limits.
soa.outcomesLine: Your cover is placed with the insurer that will offer the fullest terms for your occupation, within the caps your occupation imposes.
why: High-risk occupations restrict insurer and product choice; a pre-assessment identifies the insurer offering the best available terms before you apply.
risks: Occupational caps may leave cover below your full needs (e.g. limited benefit period or monthly cap); review if you change occupation.
alternatives: Apply to a standard insurer — discounted as cover may be declined, loaded, or offered only with a reduced benefit period for your occupation.

modules.trigger: Size TPD sum insured with a super-tax uplift (gross-up if claimed in super)

soa.strategiesLine: The TPD sum insured is set to cover your identified needs plus an uplift (e.g. 22%) to cover the tax liability that would apply should you claim while the cover is held inside your superannuation fund.
soa.outcomesLine: If you claim, the after-tax benefit still meets your identified needs because the sum insured was grossed up for the super tax.
why: A TPD benefit paid from super to a member under preservation age is taxed; grossing up the sum insured ensures the net benefit covers debts, costs and school fees as intended.
risks: If tax rates change the uplift may over- or under-compensate; the extra cover carries a small additional premium; if cover were held outside super this tax would not apply.
alternatives: Hold TPD outside super (no benefits tax, but premiums are not funded from super) or take cover without the uplift (net benefit reduced by tax).

modules.trigger: Income Protection affordability structuring — waiting & benefit period calibrated to cash/leave

soa.strategiesLine: We have recommended a 90-day waiting period as you have available cash and leave to fund 90 days of expenses, which reduces the overall cost of the cover. The benefit period is set to balance coverage and cost — the longest available where maximum protection is wanted, or a shorter (e.g. 2-year) benefit period where cash and leave reserves can bridge a longer absence.
soa.outcomesLine: Your income protection cost is minimised by matching the waiting and benefit periods to the reserves you already hold.
why: A longer waiting period and/or shorter benefit period lowers the premium; this is appropriate where you hold sufficient cash and leave to self-fund the gap.
risks: A longer wait or shorter benefit period leaves you self-funding longer — vulnerable if your cash/leave is depleted (e.g. redundancy alongside disability) or a disability extends beyond the benefit period.
alternatives: Shorter waiting period (e.g. 30 days) and/or benefit period to age 65 — maximum security at a higher premium.

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you retain [cover X], cancel [cover Y] and alter [cover Z] across your existing policies as set out below.
why: Tailors your existing cover to current needs without wholesale replacement.

modules.trigger: Any-occupation TPD definition

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend TPD cover on an Any-Occupation definition.
why: Any-Occupation is more affordable than Own-Occupation; appropriate where own-occupation is not available or not warranted.

modules.trigger: Non-occupational / homemaker TPD definition

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend TPD cover on a Non-Occupational (homemaker) definition, appropriate as you are not currently in the workforce.
why: Provides TPD protection for a non-working person where occupation-based definitions don't apply.

modules.trigger: Transfer existing cover to the recommended platform via takeover terms + top up with new cover

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend transferring your existing [industry-fund] cover to the recommended platform via takeover terms, and topping up with new recommended cover through the product insurer.
why: Takeover terms preserve your existing cover (and avoid new exclusions identified at pre-assessment) while the top-up provides the additional cover you need.
risks: Takeover terms have conditions; the new top-up cover is separately underwritten and may carry exclusions or loadings.

modules.trigger: Pre-assessment factors (smoker / health / pastimes) affecting terms

soa.strategiesLine: Note: based on pre-assessment of your [smoker status / health / pastimes], the recommended insurer offers the best available terms; cover may be subject to loadings or exclusions.

modules.trigger: Retain employer paid insurance cover

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you retain your existing employer-paid (default) insurance cover.
soa.outcomesLine: You retain a base level of protection at no cost to you through your employer-paid cover.
why: Your employer meets the cost of this cover, so retaining it provides a base level of protection at no cost to you.
risks: Employer-paid cover generally ceases when you leave your employer, and the level of cover may reduce or lapse without notice.
Default group cover has not been underwritten — terms, definitions and conditions can be altered at the insurer's discretion.
alternatives: We considered replacing the employer-paid cover with retail cover. This was not recommended as it would introduce a premium cost for cover your employer currently provides at no cost to you.

modules.trigger: Retain employer paid insurance cover + top up with new cover

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you retain your existing employer-paid (default) insurance cover and top up with new recommended cover.
soa.outcomesLine: Your combined employer-paid and top-up cover meets your identified needs at the lowest cost to your cashflow.
why: Your employer-paid cover provides a cost-free base, and the recommended top-up brings your total cover in line with your identified needs.
Structuring the top-up as new underwritten cover gives you guaranteed renewable terms on the additional amount.
risks: Employer-paid cover generally ceases when you leave your employer — your top-up alone may then be insufficient and additional cover may require underwriting at that time.
The offset/interaction between employer group cover and retail cover at claim time should be understood — benefits may not simply add together for income protection.
alternatives: We considered replacing the employer cover entirely with retail cover. This was not recommended as it would forgo cover your employer funds and increase your premium cost.

modules.trigger: Only eligible for Non-occupational TPD definition

soa.strategiesLine: Based on your circumstances you are only eligible for TPD cover on a Non-occupational definition.
soa.outcomesLine: You hold the highest TPD definition available to you, with eligibility to be reviewed if your circumstances change.
why: A Non-occupational TPD definition is the highest level of TPD cover available to you given your current work circumstances, and still provides a lump sum in the event of total and permanent disablement.
risks: A Non-occupational definition assesses disablement against everyday activities rather than your occupation, which is a stricter claims threshold than an Own- or Any-Occupation definition.
alternatives: Own-Occupation and Any-Occupation TPD definitions were considered but are not available to you based on your current circumstances. We will review your eligibility if your circumstances change.

modules.trigger: Only eligible for Homemaker TPD definition

soa.strategiesLine: Based on your circumstances you are only eligible for TPD cover on a Homemaker definition.
soa.outcomesLine: You hold the highest TPD definition available to you, with eligibility to be reviewed if you return to paid employment.
why: A Homemaker TPD definition is the highest level of TPD cover available to you while not in paid employment, and still provides a lump sum in the event of total and permanent disablement.
risks: A Homemaker definition assesses disablement against the ability to perform normal domestic duties rather than an occupation, which is a stricter claims threshold than occupation-based definitions.
alternatives: Own-Occupation and Any-Occupation TPD definitions were considered but are not available to you based on your current circumstances. We will review your eligibility if you return to paid employment.

modules.trigger: Income Protection increasing claims (CPI) not available

soa.strategiesLine: Please note an increasing-claims (CPI-indexed) benefit is not available on the recommended income protection cover.
soa.outcomesLine: You understand the recommended income protection benefit is not CPI-indexed during a claim.
why: Disclosing this limitation ensures you understand that benefit payments during a long claim will not be indexed to inflation under the recommended policy.
risks: During an extended claim, the real value of your monthly benefit will reduce over time as it is not indexed to CPI.
alternatives: We considered policies offering an increasing-claims option. On balance, the recommended policy was preferred for its overall terms and pricing; the absence of CPI indexation was weighed in that comparison.

modules.trigger: Pre-assessment factors: health disclosure

soa.strategiesLine: Note: based on pre-assessment of your health disclosures, cover may be subject to loadings or exclusions.
soa.outcomesLine: Your cover has been recommended with your health pre-assessment factored in, setting clear expectations on terms.
why: Pre-assessing your health disclosures with insurers before application sets clear expectations on terms and avoids surprises at underwriting.
risks: Final underwriting may apply premium loadings or exclusions that differ from the pre-assessment indication.
Non-disclosure of health matters can void cover at claim time — full and accurate disclosure is essential.
alternatives: We considered insurers who indicated less favourable pre-assessment terms for your health disclosures; the recommended insurer offered the most favourable indicative terms.

modules.trigger: Pre-assessment factors: pastimes

soa.strategiesLine: Note: based on pre-assessment of your pastimes/pursuits, cover may be subject to loadings or exclusions.
soa.outcomesLine: Your cover has been recommended with your pastimes pre-assessment factored in, setting clear expectations on terms.
why: Pre-assessing your pastimes and pursuits with insurers before application sets clear expectations on terms and avoids surprises at underwriting.
risks: Final underwriting may apply premium loadings or exclusions for hazardous pastimes that differ from the pre-assessment indication.
Taking up new hazardous pursuits after cover commences may not be covered — check policy terms before participating.
alternatives: We considered insurers who indicated less favourable pre-assessment terms for your pastimes; the recommended insurer offered the most favourable indicative terms.

You will benefit from a competitive interest rate within the Macquarie Cash Management Account.

why: A cash buffer provides liquidity and peace of mind for unexpected expenses.

modules.trigger: Prepare / review your Will

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend that you approach a solicitor to ensure that you have a valid and updated Will in place.
soa.outcomesLine: A current Will ensures your assets are distributed according to your wishes.
why: Control — a Will names the beneficiaries who receive your assets and on what terms, and appoints an executor to manage the distribution.
Intestacy — without a valid Will, your assets would be distributed by a prescribed government formula and possibly not in accordance with your wishes.
Relevance — a Will should be updated at least every three years and after any major change in circumstances.
risks: If you fail to update your Will following marriage or divorce it may be rendered invalid, possibly resulting in parts of your estate not being distributed according to your wishes.
alternatives: (estate documents are essential — no alternative presented)

modules.trigger: Prepare / review Power of Attorney

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend that you approach a solicitor to ensure that you have a valid and updated Power of Attorney in place.
soa.outcomesLine: A Power of Attorney ensures someone you trust can manage your affairs if you are unable to.
why: A Power of Attorney allows a trusted person to make financial/legal decisions on your behalf if you are unable to do so.
risks: A Power of Attorney is a significant document granting authority to act on your behalf — ensure you appoint someone you trust.
alternatives: (estate documents are essential — no alternative presented)

modules.trigger: Non-lapsing binding death benefit nomination (super)

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you choose a non-lapsing binding death nomination within your superannuation funds.
soa.outcomesLine: A binding nomination ensures your super death benefit is paid according to your wishes.
why: A non-lapsing binding nomination binds the trustee to pay your super death benefit according to your wishes and remains in force until amended or revoked (subject to the fund's Trust Deed).
Death benefit payment option — you can nominate dependants under the non-lapsing binding election, or you can select an automatic reversionary pension under the pension plan.
risks: When you die, the proceeds from your superannuation fund may be subject to tax if paid as a lump sum to non-dependants. (delete if the fund cannot offer this nomination)

modules.trigger: Testamentary trust

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend that you contact a solicitor to ensure that you have a valid and updated testamentary trust in place.
soa.outcomesLine: A testamentary trust can provide tax‑effective and protected distribution of your estate.
why: Tax Benefits — a testamentary trust allows trustees to distribute and split the income of the trust with tax planning in mind.
Asset Protection — the trust holds the title to the trust's assets (rather than the beneficiaries directly), allowing the trust to protect assets from any litigation, bankruptcy or legal action.

Flexibility — a testamentary trust can provide great flexibility to suit individual circumstances. For example, it is possible to restrict access to assets or distributions to a particular beneficiary.
risks: Your solicitor may charge a fee to review / update your Wills and/or Powers of Attorney.
Estate planning laws vary between Australian states and territories as well as between countries. For this reason, it is important to ensure that your Will is valid for the state in which you live.
A Will does not expire and it is therefore important to have it reviewed and updated if or when your situation changes.
Should you fail to update your Will following marriage or divorce it will render it invalid, possibly resulting in parts of your estate not being distributed according to your wishes.
alternatives: Distribute the estate directly via the Will — discounted where the tax and asset-protection benefits of a testamentary trust are valuable to your beneficiaries.

modules.trigger: Apply for the Centrelink Age Pension (retirement trigger)
modules.scopeGate: Client(s) reaching/at Age Pension age and retiring or reducing work

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend that next financial year, when you retire or reduce your work, you apply for the Centrelink Age Pension.
soa.outcomesLine: You access government income support to supplement your pension drawdowns once retired.
why: On full retirement you may be entitled to a meaningful fortnightly payment as a homeowner, supplementing your account-based pension income and reducing the drawdown pressure on your super.

Eligibility for the Age Pension may also entitle you to additional Commonwealth concessions, including the Pensioner Concession Card — which may provide access to subsidised pharmaceutical costs under the PBS and other state-based concessions. Eligibility is determined by Services Australia and subject to ongoing assessment.
risks: Entitlement depends on the assets and income tests at the time; rates and thresholds are subject to change and indexation.
alternatives: Rely solely on pension drawdowns — discounted as it forgoes available government support.

modules.trigger: Use the My Wealth Portal

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you utilise the My Wealth Portal to track all your investments and cashflow.
soa.outcomesLine: Consolidating your finances in one place streamlines administration and keeps you on track.
why: The My Wealth Portal will allow you to consolidate your financial world into one place, streamlining administration.
The My Wealth Portal includes an automated budgeting system which provides clarity and allows you to take control of your cashflow.
Allows you to build personalised cash flow targets and goals which keep you accountable over time.
risks: (administrative tool — no downside)

modules.trigger: Establish your investments through the recommended platform

soa.strategiesLine: We recommend you establish your new [investment / superannuation] account through the [Hub24 Choice / Netwealth / Colonial First State Edge] platform.
soa.outcomesLine: Using the recommended platform provides access to the recommended investment menu with competitive administration costs.

modules.trigger: Investment company / bucket company
